scenes.text: Hello little friends! I'm part of the Rescue Pup Crew, and today we're going to explore something super exciting called confidence. Are you ready to join me on this adventure? Confidence is like a special power that helps us try new things and feel proud of ourselves. It's what makes us brave when we try to learn something new, like tying our shoes or riding a bike. Let's discover how we can all be confident together!

Now, let's think about what confidence really means. Confidence is when you believe in yourself, even when things seem a little tricky. Remember when you first learned to brush your teeth all by yourself? That took confidence! It's about knowing you can do something if you try, and that it's okay to make mistakes along the way. Everyone learns at their own pace, and that's perfectly fine. The important thing is to keep trying and believe in your abilities.

Let's practice building our confidence with a simple exercise. Imagine you're about to do something new, like drawing a picture. First, take a deep breath in, and then let it out slowly. Doesn't that feel calming? Now, say to yourself, 'I can do this!' It's like giving yourself a little pep talk. This helps you feel ready and brave to start your task. Remember, confidence grows with practice, just like learning to ride your bike!

Great job! You're already on your way to being more confident. Let's try something fun together. Think of something you'd like to do, like building a block tower. As you build, say, 'I am strong and capable!' If the tower falls, that's okay. You can always try again. Each time you try, your confidence gets a little stronger. Just like when we help someone in need, every small step counts towards success.

Remember when we talked about how confidence helps us try new things? It's also important to celebrate our achievements, no matter how small they seem. Like when you put your toys away or help set the table. Each time you do something well, give yourself a little cheer. Say, 'I did it!' Celebrating helps us feel good and encourages us to keep going. Being proud of yourself is a big part of building confidence.

Now let's take a moment to think about a time when you felt really proud of yourself. Maybe it was when you learned to tie your shoes or draw a picture. Close your eyes and remember how happy and confident that moment made you feel. This is your confidence memory. Whenever you feel unsure, you can think back to this moment, and it will remind you that you can do amazing things. Let's keep that feeling with us as we move forward.

Can you think of a new thing you'd like to try? Maybe it's learning a new game or helping in the kitchen. What do you think would help you feel confident trying it? Is it asking for help from a grown-up, or maybe practicing a little each day? Confidence grows when we take small steps and don't give up. Let's think about this together and share our ideas. What new adventure might you embark on with a little more confidence today?

Let's continue to think about how confidence helps us in different situations. Imagine being on a playground and wanting to join a new game. Confidence is what helps you walk over and ask to play. It might feel a bit scary at first, but remember, everyone loves making new friends. You can say, 'Hi, can I join your game?' Most times, they'll be happy to have you. Being confident helps you make new friends and have more fun!

You're doing fantastic! Let's take a moment to breathe deeply again. Inhale slowly and let it out. Wonderful! Breathing helps calm our minds and bodies, making it easier to feel confident. When you're calm, it's easier to remember all the amazing things you can do. Keep practicing your breathing whenever you need a little boost of courage. Remember, you're brave, and you can do anything you set your mind to!

Now, let's talk about how asking for help can also be a sign of confidence. Sometimes, we need a little support to learn something new, and that's okay. Like when you're building a puzzle and need a friend to help find a piece. Asking for help shows you believe in teamwork and are confident enough to know when to seek help. It's a smart way to learn and grow, and it makes our friendships even stronger.

Remember when we talked about celebrating our achievements? It's also important to recognize the efforts of others. If you see a friend doing something brave, like trying the slide for the first time, give them a cheer. Say, 'Great job!' This helps them feel confident too. Encouraging others is a wonderful way to build confidence in yourself and others. It's all about spreading positivity and building each other up.

Have you ever felt nervous about something new, like going to a new school or meeting new people? What do you think could help you feel more confident in those situations? Maybe bringing a favorite toy or having a friend by your side? Let's think about what makes us feel safe and confident when trying new things. Sharing our thoughts can help us find new ways to be brave together.

Now let's talk about how practice makes us more confident. Just like when you learn to ride a bike, the more you practice, the more confident you become. It's the same with anything new, like learning a new song or dance. Practicing helps you feel more comfortable and sure of yourself. Remember, even if it's a little tricky at first, you get better with each try. Keep practicing, and confidence will follow!

You're doing amazing, and I'm so proud of you! Let's keep building our confidence by trying new things every day. Whether it's drawing a new picture or helping with chores, each small step counts. Remember, confidence is like a muscle—the more you use it, the stronger it gets. Keep believing in yourself, and you'll achieve great things. You're a star, and I can't wait to see all the wonderful things you'll do!

Thank you for joining me on this exciting confidence adventure! Remember, confidence is your special power that helps you try new things and feel proud. Keep practicing your breathing, celebrating your successes, and asking for help when needed. You're already on your way to being a confident superstar. I'm so proud of you, and I know you'll continue to shine bright. Until next time, keep believing in yourself and have fun exploring new adventures!
